info.title: Pando API
info.description:
The HTTP API of a Pando installation. The console, the `pando` CLI and the MCP server are clients of it, and none of them can do anything it cannot (R-261).

Authenticate with a token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or the session cookie the console signs in with. A failed request answers with the error envelope: a stable `code` to branch on, a `message` to show, and often a `remedy`.

A field listed as required is always present in a response. A request may leave out any field it does not need; Pando answers `VALID_INVALID` naming what is missing.

Generated from the code by `make reference`.

host.description: The address Pando's console is reached at.

get.summary: The adapters configured here and what they can currently do — live capabilities, not stored configuration.
get.description:
The adapters configured here and what they can currently do — live capabilities, not stored configuration. Names which credentials are set, never their values. `pending_restart` marks one saved since Pando started, which is not yet what runs; `restart_needed` says any is. A routing adapter Pando runs a process in front of itself for — Traefik, cloudflared — has `edge`: whether it is running, and why not to whoever may change it (R-174). An image registry is signed in to for its health, and has `capabilities` like a runtime.

Needs `install.view`.

post.summary: Configure an adapter.
post.description:
Configure an adapter. Settings go in config; credentials such as an API key go in credentials, which is write-only and stored encrypted. A source connection (category `source`) and an image registry (category `image_registry`) are used from the moment they are saved, with no restart; an image registry Pando could not push to is refused before it is saved. An audit sink (category `audit_sink`) is used from the next delivery pass too, is refused when its settings are, and needs `install.audit.export` as well, because it sends the audit log off the installation (R-385).

Needs `install.adapters.manage`.

additionalProperties.description: Always `[redacted]`: a secret's value is never written to a response (R-194).

get.summary: The kinds of adapter this build of Pando can run, and the settings each takes — which are credentials (write-only, stored encrypted), which are required, the default each takes when left empty or an example, and which are `advanced`: less common, never required, always with a default, and asked for apart from the rest.
get.description: Needs `install.view`.

post.summary: Draft a custom role and a group from a description, with verbs from the catalog only.
post.description:

Needs `install.users.manage`.

post.summary: Turn a question into audit filters, run them, and summarize what they found.
post.description:
Turn a question into audit filters, run them, and summarize what they found. Body: `question`. The filters are ordinary GET /audit parameters (R-345).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

post.summary: Propose host policy from a description: the document as it would be saved, and each change.
post.description:
Propose host policy from a description: the document as it would be saved, and each change. Fields fixed in the startup configuration are declined, naming where. Body: `description`, and `proposed` with the document so far to refine it. Save it with PUT /policy (R-344).

post.description: Answer a "How can I…" question from this reference, citing the endpoints, commands and tools it relies on. Body: `question`. Describes; does nothing (R-346).

get.summary: Deploys waiting for approval on every app you can see, oldest first: each deployment with `app_name`, `app_slug`, its `approval_reasons`, the `approvals` so far, and `can_decide` — whether you may approve or reject it.
get.description: Deploys waiting for approval on every app you can see, oldest first: each deployment with `app_name`, `app_slug`, its `approval_reasons`, the `approvals` so far, and `can_decide` — whether you may approve or reject it. `limit` (default 100, at most 500) and `cursor` page; `next_cursor` continues, and a page can hold fewer than `limit` and still have one.

get.summary: The apps you can administer.
get.description: The apps you can administer. Each carries `detection` — its status, and its stage while running — once it has been through detection. Newest first, a page at a time: `limit` (default 100, at most 500), `cursor` (the previous page's `next_cursor`, which is empty after the last page), `q` to match the name or slug, and `id`, repeatable, to read only those apps. `total` counts the matches exactly up to 10,000; past that it is 10,000 and `total_is_lower_bound` is true (O-53).

post.summary: Create an app.
post.description:
Create an app. `source` is `{type: git, url, ref, connection}` for a repository — `connection` optional, the source connection to read a private one with; left out, the one covering the address most closely is used — `{type: image, image, credential}` for an image that is already built (`credential` optional, for a private one: see PUT /registry-credential), or `{type: upload}` for files sent next with POST /source. Checked against the source allowlist before anything is fetched (R-092), then the repository is checked to be readable, so a private one no connection can read is refused with `VALID_SOURCE_UNREADABLE` saying why (R-091). Returns immediately in draft while detection runs; follow it with GET /detection and `wait`.

Needs `app.create`.

schema.description: Makes a retry of this request return the first response rather than act twice. Also accepted as `idempotency_key` in the body.

202.description: Accepted: the work continues after the response.

delete.summary: Delete an app.
delete.description:
Delete an app. With storage, `backup=true` keeps a final copy and `force=true` discards it; without either, the request is refused so the decision is taken rather than assumed (R-204, R-205). When host policy has `require_backup_before_destroy`, `force=true` is refused for an app with storage (R-284).

Needs `app.delete`.

get.summary: One app: name, source, state and pinned spec; `detection` — its status, and its stage while running — once it has been through detection; and `last_backup`, its last daily backup attempt.
get.description: Needs `app.view`.

put.summary: Change the automatic deploy settings: `enabled`, `trigger` (`branch_updated`, the default, or `release_tagged`), `branch` (empty follows the branch the app was deployed from) and `tag_pattern` (a glob such as `release-*`; empty counts tags like `v1.2.3` as releases).
put.description:
Change the automatic deploy settings: `enabled`, `trigger` (`branch_updated`, the default, or `release_tagged`), `branch` (empty follows the branch the app was deployed from) and `tag_pattern` (a glob such as `release-*`; empty counts tags like `v1.2.3` as releases). Writes a revision the next deploy ships; 200 with `changed: false` when nothing changes. Refused while the app's deploys need approval (R-158).

Needs `app.spec.edit`.

post.summary: Where a git host sends push and release events (R-142): GitHub's format, `X-GitHub-Event` and `X-Hub-Signature-256` signed with the app's webhook secret.
post.description: Where a git host sends push and release events (R-142): GitHub's format, `X-GitHub-Event` and `X-Hub-Signature-256` signed with the app's webhook secret. A verified delivery about what the app watches starts a check (202); one about something else is ignored (200). The check reads the repository itself, so nothing in the payload decides what deploys. Public: the signature is the credential.

schema.description: The event as GitHub sends it, signed in `X-Hub-Signature-256`.

202.description: Accepted: the work continues after the response.

get.summary: Every deploy of this app, newest first.
get.description:
Every deploy of this app, newest first. One waiting in the queue for a build slot carries `queue_position`: how many queued deploys are ahead of it, 0 for the next.

Needs `app.view`.

post.summary: Deploy.
post.description:
Deploy. Returns 202 with the deployment; the build runs behind it. When the deploy needs approval (R-154) it comes back `awaiting_approval` instead, the app is left as it is, the people who can approve are told, and any older request for the app still waiting is superseded. Retrying with the same idempotency key replays the first answer rather than deploying twice (R-262).

Needs `app.deploy`.

schema.description: Makes a retry of this request return the first response rather than act twice. Also accepted as `idempotency_key` in the body.

202.description: Accepted: the work continues after the response.

post.summary: Deploy the last revision that ran successfully, or the revision `to` names.
post.description:
Deploy the last revision that ran successfully, or the revision `to` names. Rolling back to a revision that ran successfully before never needs approval (R-157).

Needs `app.deploy`.

schema.description: Makes a retry of this request return the first response rather than act twice. Also accepted as `idempotency_key` in the body.

202.description: Accepted: the work continues after the response.

get.summary: One deploy: what it shipped, and how it ended.
get.description:
One deploy: what it shipped, and how it ended. One that needed approval carries `approvals_required`, `approval_expires_at`, `approval_reasons`, the `approvals` so far and, while it waits, `can_decide`. One waiting in the queue for a build slot carries `queue_position`, how many are ahead of it.

Needs `app.view`.

post.summary: Approve a deploy that is waiting for approval, with an optional `comment`.
post.description:
Approve a deploy that is waiting for approval, with an optional `comment`. Takes `install.deploys.approve`, or `app.deploy.approve` on this app; either may approve its holder's own request (R-155). The last approval it needs plans it again and starts it: 200 with the deployment, `pending` once started and still `awaiting_approval` while it needs more. Refused while another deploy of the app is running; the request keeps waiting.

Needs `app.view`.

get.summary: The deploy's output as server-sent events, flushed per line while it runs (R-170).
get.description:
The deploy's output as server-sent events, flushed per line while it runs (R-170). While the deploy waits in the queue, a line saying how many deploys are ahead of it, again each time that changes; then the deploy's own output in the same stream.

Needs `app.logs.read`.

post.summary: Reject a deploy that is waiting for approval, with an optional `comment`.
post.description:
Reject a deploy that is waiting for approval, with an optional `comment`. One rejection ends the request (R-156). The same permissions as approving.

Needs `app.view`.

get.summary: What Pando worked out about the repository: the winning bid, its evidence, the runners-up and any outstanding questions.
get.description:
What Pando worked out about the repository: the winning bid, its evidence, the runners-up and any outstanding questions. While `status` is `running`, `stage` is one of fetching, detecting, trying, scanning or screening, and `elapsed_seconds` how long it has been going. `wait` (seconds, up to 60) holds the answer until detection reaches a new stage or finishes.

Needs `app.view`.

post.summary: Accept the proposal, writing a spec revision and pinning it.
post.description:
Accept the proposal, writing a spec revision and pinning it. `values` sets variables in the same step — `{key, value, secret?, workload?}` each; a secret goes to the secrets adapter and needs app.secrets.write. Accepting over a configured app needs `confirm`.

Needs `app.spec.edit`.

post.summary: Answer detection's questions.
post.description:
Answer detection's questions. Each answer is a fact detection could not find, not a preference.

Needs `app.spec.edit`.

get.description: Needs `app.view`.

post.description:

get.summary: The installation's egress rules (`install`: mode, list, private-address blocking, and what loosening them needs), the rules the pinned spec runs with, merged, with every loosening and what it needs (`effective`), the pinned spec's own egress settings (`spec`), and which revision those are (`revision`).

The installation's egress rules (`install`: mode, list, private-address blocking, and what loosening them needs), the rules the pinned spec runs with, merged, with every loosening and what it needs (`effective`), the pinned spec's own egress settings (`spec`), and which revision those are (`revision`). `?revision=N`, or `?revision=latest` for the newest, reads that revision instead — what a saved change not yet deployed would run with. put.description:
Set the app's tile image. The body is the image itself — PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 256 KB. SVG is refused (R-340).

get.summary: Whether Pando stops or deletes this app when nobody uses it (R-393 – R-397): its own `stop_days` and `delete_days` (null is the installation's, 0 is off), the installation's, the ones in force, `last_activity_at`, and `stops_at` and `deletes_at` if nothing happens before then.
get.description:
Whether Pando stops or deletes this app when nobody uses it (R-393 – R-397): its own `stop_days` and `delete_days` (null is the installation's, 0 is off), the installation's, the ones in force, `last_activity_at`, and `stops_at` and `deletes_at` if nothing happens before then. `stopped_for_idle` says Pando stopped it.

Needs `app.view`.

put.summary: Set this app's own `stop_days` and `delete_days`: a number of days, 0 to turn it off, or null for the installation's.
put.description:
Set this app's own `stop_days` and `delete_days`: a number of days, 0 to turn it off, or null for the installation's. Deleting has to come later than stopping. App settings, not spec: no revision is written and nothing is deployed (R-397). Withdraws any notice already given.

Needs `app.spec.edit`.

get.summary: The app's own output, from the runtime, as plain text.
get.description:
The app's own output, from the runtime, as plain text. `tail` sets how many of the most recent lines (default 200, at most 5000; a larger number is read as 5000); `workload` picks which part of the app, defaulting to the primary one. `follow=true` keeps the response open and adds each new line as it is printed, from the same shared stream as /logs/stream, starting from the recent lines that stream holds rather than from `tail`.

Needs `app.logs.read`.

get.summary: The app's own output live, as server-sent events (O-51).
get.description:
The app's own output live, as server-sent events (O-51). `workload` picks the part, defaulting to the primary one. Opens with `event: reset` and up to the last 1000 lines, then sends each new line as a `data:` event; `event: notice` reports the runtime's stream ending (a restart) and being reconnected. Access is checked again every two minutes: the stream ends with `event: revoked` when it no longer holds, and a client must not reconnect after it; `event: lagged` means the client fell too far behind and may reconnect. Every viewer of a part on one Pando server shares one stream from the runtime.

Needs `app.logs.read`.

200.description: Server-sent events: each `data:` line is a line of the app's output.

get.summary: The name of an app that asks for a passcode, for its passcode page.
get.description: The name of an app that asks for a passcode, for its passcode page. Public; not-found for any other app (R-075a).

post.description: Enter an app's passcode (`passcode`). Right, and the browser is let in for a day by a cookie the app never sees; ten wrong tries in fifteen minutes and it waits. Public (R-075a).

put.description:

Writes a revision the next deploy ships. A change needs `confirm: true`, since the old address stops working; a mode the adapter does not default to also needs app.routing.override (R-163). post.description:
Send an app's files as its source: a gzipped tar of the app's directory (Content-Type `application/gzip`, at most 256 MB), paths relative to its root. A single index.html is enough for a static site. get.summary: Every spec revision, and which one is pinned.
get.description:
Every spec revision, and which one is pinned. Revisions are append-only (R-152).

Needs `app.view`.

post.summary: Write a new spec revision.
post.description:
Write a new spec revision. It does not deploy and does not become pinned. A routing mode other than its adapter's default, where the app did not already have one, also needs app.routing.override (R-163). A change to `egress` needs app.egress.tighten or app.egress.loosen; one that newly loosens the installation's egress rules needs app.egress.loosen where policy gates loosening by verb, is refused with PLAN_EGRESS_LOOSENING_FORBIDDEN where policy forbids it, and makes the next deploy need approval where policy says so (R-183, R-184). Turning on automatic deploys while the app's deploys need approval is refused (R-158). With `?dry_run=true` nothing is written: the same checks run and refuse with the same errors, and an accepted spec answers 200 with the egress rules it would run with, what it newly loosens, and whether deploying it would need approval and why.

Needs `app.spec.edit`.

get.description: Needs `app.view`.

get.summary: The audit log, newest first.
get.description:
The audit log, newest first. Filters combine: `action` (a prefix), `principal_id` (who did it, including through a token), `principal_kind` (user, token, system or anonymous), `app_id`, `target_kind` and `target_id` (what it was done to), `involving` (an ID that is the actor or the target — everything to do with one account), and `since`/`until` (RFC 3339; since inclusive, until exclusive). Pages with `before`. Append-only: no endpoint edits or deletes an event, and the database refuses it too (R-027). Each event carries `outcome` (success, denied or failed), `source_ip`, `peer_ip`, `user_agent`, `actor_name`, `actor_email` and `schema_version` (R-379). Reading the log is itself audited, as `audit.read` (R-388).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: The months of the audit log past retention, archived and removed from the live log (R-347).
get.description:
The months of the audit log past retention, archived and removed from the live log (R-347). Each with its manifest: `month`, `row_count`, `first_id` and `last_id`, `first_at` and `last_at`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, and where it is kept — `adapter_ref` when exported to a backup destination, absent when Pando keeps it. Retention is host policy's `audit_retention_months` (at least 3) and `audit_archive` (keep, export or off).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: Download one archived month: gzipped JSON lines, one audit event per line with every field the live log held.
get.description:
Download one archived month: gzipped JSON lines, one audit event per line with every field the live log held. `Repr-Digest` carries its SHA-256, the same as the manifest's `sha256`. Audited as `audit.archive.download` (R-388).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: Any range of the live log as gzipped JSON lines, in commit order (R-387): `since` and `until` (RFC 3339), `action` and `exclude` prefixes, and `format` `native` (the archive's line format) or `ocsf`.
get.description:
Any range of the live log as gzipped JSON lines, in commit order (R-387): `since` and `until` (RFC 3339), `action` and `exclude` prefixes, and `format` `native` (the archive's line format) or `ocsf`. When the range reaches before the live log, `Pando-Audit-Live-From` names its oldest event's time, and archives hold the rest. Audited as `audit.export`.

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: Every audit sink — a destination the log is pushed to as it is written (R-382) — with what it sends where (`transport`, `endpoint`, `format`, `actions`, `exclude`, and `disclosure`, the sentence the console shows), its last delivered event (`cursor_at`, `delivered_at`, `delivered_count`), `backlog`, `last_error`, `failing_since`, `disabled_at` and `disabled_reason` when Pando turned it off, and `gap_from`/`gap_to` for a range it missed (R-383, R-386).
get.description:
Every audit sink — a destination the log is pushed to as it is written (R-382) — with what it sends where (`transport`, `endpoint`, `format`, `actions`, `exclude`, and `disclosure`, the sentence the console shows), its last delivered event (`cursor_at`, `delivered_at`, `delivered_count`), `backlog`, `last_error`, `failing_since`, `disabled_at` and `disabled_reason` when Pando turned it off, and `gap_from`/`gap_to` for a range it missed (R-383, R-386). Audit sinks are adapters of category `audit_sink`, created with `POST /adapters`, which needs `install.audit.export` for them (R-385).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: The audit log in commit order, oldest first, from a cursor (R-381): for a collector that must miss nothing across restarts, upgrades and replicas.
get.description:
The audit log in commit order, oldest first, from a cursor (R-381): for a collector that must miss nothing across restarts, upgrades and replicas. `after` is the `cursor` a previous read returned; empty starts at the oldest event in the live log, and `now` after the newest. `limit` (default 500, at most 1000); `wait` (0–60 seconds) holds the request until an event arrives; `action` and `exclude` are repeatable prefixes, and the cursor moves past what they drop; `format` is `native` (the archive's line format) or `ocsf`. Answers `events`, `cursor` and `caught_up`. Delivery is at least once: an event's `id` is its idempotency key. Audited as `audit.read` at most once an hour per reader (R-388).

Needs `install.audit.read`.

get.summary: Whether a newer Pando is released (R-351): `current`, `latest`, `available`, and `releases`, each version after the running one, newest first, with its changelog section as `notes` and `security` and `breaking` marked.
get.description:
Whether a newer Pando is released (R-351): `current`, `latest`, `available`, and `releases`, each version after the running one, newest first, with its changelog section as `notes` and `security` and `breaking` marked. `upgrade` says how to move this installation to `latest`. `enabled` and `channel` are host policy's `disable_update_check` and `update_channel`; while the check is off Pando sends no request and reports nothing. `error` says why the last check failed. Every response to a signed-in caller carries the server's version as `Pando-Version`.

Needs `install.view`.

get.summary: What an in-place upgrade to `?version=` would do (R-355, R-360): `possible`, and when not, `reasons`, each saying what to change; `image`, how Pando's deployment names its image, and `tag`, the moving tag the upgrade points at the new image; `breaking`, the versions in between that may break what works now, with their notes, which make `confirm_breaking` necessary; and `note`, that every app is unreachable while Pando restarts.
get.description: Needs `install.view`.

post.summary: Upgrade Pando in place (R-355 – R-360).
post.description:
Upgrade Pando in place (R-355 – R-360). Body: `version`; `passphrase` for the full backup taken first, or `skip_backup: true` to go without one, which is audited; and `confirm_breaking`, the version again, when the plan lists `breaking` versions. The image's signature is verified before anything else, and Pando refuses one that does not verify. Answers 202 with the upgrade: a helper then stops Pando, copies its database, starts the new version and waits for it to be ready, and puts the previous version and database back if it is not. Every app is unreachable while Pando restarts. `GET /upgrade/last` has the outcome once Pando is back.

Needs `install.upgrade`.

202.description: Accepted: the work continues after the response.

get.summary: The most recent in-place upgrade, as `upgrade`, or null: `from`, `to`, `state` (`running`, `succeeded`, `rolled_back` or `failed`), `reason`, the new version's last log lines when it was rolled back, `backup_id` or `skip_backup`, and whether the rollback copy of the database is still kept (`snapshot_gone`, after 24 hours healthy).
get.description: Needs `install.view`.

get.summary: The accounts on this installation, newest first, each with its `install_role_id`.
get.description:
The accounts on this installation, newest first, each with its `install_role_id`. `limit` (default 100, at most 500) and `cursor` page; `next_cursor` continues; `q` matches the username, display name or email; `id`, repeatable, reads only those accounts; `total` counts the matches exactly up to 10,000; past that it is 10,000 and `total_is_lower_bound` is true (O-53).

Needs `install.view`.

patch.description:
Change an account: any of `username`, `display_name`, `email` and `status`. Username and email only on a local account; a username only with this verb, even your own. Suspension is not deletion (R-049). Your own name and email need no verb.

get.description:
How many apps an account may own (R-244): `limit` (0 is unlimited), where it comes from (`source`: user, group or policy, with `group_id` and `group_name` for a group), how many it owns (`owned`), and the value set on the account itself (`max_apps`, null when none is). Your own needs no verb.

Needs `install.users.manage`.

put.summary: Set `max_apps` on an account: a number, 0 for unlimited, or null to clear it.
put.description:
Set `max_apps` on an account: a number, 0 for unlimited, or null to clear it. It applies whatever the account's groups say. Lowering it below what the account owns removes nothing; it refuses the next app (R-244).

Needs `install.users.manage`.

get.summary: The apps an account has something on: its role for managing each, directly or through a group, whether it can use each, and whether you can change that (`can_manage`).
get.description:
The apps an account has something on: its role for managing each, directly or through a group, whether it can use each, and whether you can change that (`can_manage`). Only apps you can see are listed. Your own needs nothing. By app name, a page of apps at a time: `limit` (default 100, at most 500) and `cursor` page; `next_cursor` continues, and a page can hold fewer apps than the limit when some are ones you cannot see.

Needs `install.view`.

get.description: The external identities that sign in to an account: which provider, its ID for the person, whether it is where the account came from, and whether SCIM manages it. Your own, or anyone's with install.view.

post.summary: Link a provider's identity (`adapter_id`, `external_id`) to an account, so it signs in there.
post.description:
Link a provider's identity (`adapter_id`, `external_id`) to an account, so it signs in there. Adds an alias and never merges accounts (O-1). If it already signs in to another account, `replace_account: true` moves it, and that account is kept, suspended, as an alias.

Needs `install.users.manage`.

post.summary: Reset another local account's password (`password`), ending every session it holds.
post.description:
Reset another local account's password (`password`), ending every session it holds. `must_change_password` defaults to true: whoever set it hands it over, and its holder chooses their own at the next sign-in. Your own is `POST /me/password`.

Needs `install.users.manage`.

delete.summary: Take an installation role away.
delete.description:
Take an installation role away. The last administrator cannot be demoted.

Needs `install.users.manage`.

put.summary: Give an account an installation role.
put.description:
Give an account an installation role. Deliberately not a field on PATCH: changing someone's status and changing their power are different acts.

Needs `install.users.manage`.

code.description:
A stable code to branch on. Renaming one is a breaking change.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALID_DANGLING_MOUNT` | 400 | A workload mounts a volume the spec does not declare. |
| `VALID_DANGLING_SLOT_REF` | 400 | The spec refers to a slot it does not declare. |
| `VALID_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE` | 400 | The workloads depend on each other in a cycle. |
| `VALID_ENV_AMBIGUOUS` | 400 | An environment variable is set twice with different values. |
| `VALID_INVALID` | 400 | The request or spec is malformed. |
| `VALID_PRIMARY_WORKLOAD` | 400 | A spec must name exactly one primary workload. |
| `VALID_SOURCE_UNREADABLE` | 400 | Pando could not read the repository: it is private or missing and no source connection covers it, or the connection's credential was refused (R-091). |
| `VALID_UNKNOWN_EVENT` | 400 | A subscription names an event, or a pattern, that matches no event in the catalog (R-364). |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | The credential presented is not valid. |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | No credential was presented, or the session has expired. |
| `AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID` | 401 | The token is unknown, revoked or expired. |
| `AUTH_TOKEN_ORPHANED` | 401 | The token's owner was suspended or deleted, so the token no longer resolves to anyone (R-059). |
| `PERM_CROSS_ORIGIN` | 403 | A change sent with a browser's Pando sign-in from a page on another origin, such as an app's. Send it from the console, or with an API token. |
| `PERM_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but not permitted to do this. |
| `PERM_PASSCODE_REQUIRED` | 403 | The app is shared with everyone who knows its passcode, and this request has not shown it. A browser is sent to the passcode page; entering it there lets the visitor in. |
| `PERM_VERB_REQUIRED` | 403 | The caller holds no grant carrying the verb this action needs. |
| `POLICY_ANONYMOUS_GRANT_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Host policy does not allow apps to be shared with everyone (R-076). |
| `POLICY_APP_LIMIT_REACHED` | 403 | The person who would own the new app already owns as many apps as their limit allows. The message names the limit and where it is set (R-244). |
| `POLICY_BACKUP_REQUIRED` | 403 | Host policy requires a final backup before an app with storage is deleted, and the request said to delete without one (R-284). |
| `POLICY_EXEC_DISABLED` | 403 | Host policy has turned off terminal access, including for an app's owner (R-085). |
| `POLICY_SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED` | 403 | Host policy does not allow apps from this source (R-092). |
| `POLICY_WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESS` | 403 | A webhook points at a private, loopback or link-local address, and host policy does not allow that (R-372). |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No such object, or none the caller may see. |
| `CAPACITY_NO_FREE_PORT` | 409 | Port-mode routing has no free port in the configured range. |
| `CAPACITY_WOULD_OVERSUBSCRIBE` | 409 | Running this would commit more of the host than is left (R-242). |
| `PLAN_ADAPTER_NOT_CONFIGURED` | 409 | The spec names an adapter this installation does not have. |
| `PLAN_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` | 409 | The spec asks for something the chosen adapter does not do (R-254). |
| `PLAN_COMPOSE_CONSTRUCT_REJECTED` | 409 | The compose file uses a construct Pando will not translate (R-099). |
| `PLAN_EGRESS_LOOSENING_FORBIDDEN` | 409 | The app loosens the installation's egress rules, and host policy says no app may (R-183). |
| `PLAN_IMAGE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | 409 | The app's image has no build for the operating system and CPU architecture this server runs, so it cannot start here. |
| `PLAN_NO_ADAPTER_MEETS_POLICY` | 409 | No configured adapter can satisfy this spec under host policy (R-024, R-114). |
| `PLAN_SECURITY_BELOW_THRESHOLD` | 409 | This installation requires a security score, and this app is below it or has never been scanned (R-314). |
| `PLAN_SLOT_UNFILLED` | 409 | A required dependency has nothing filling it, so the deploy would start an app that cannot connect (R-132). |
| `STATE_ADDRESS_TAKEN` | 409 | Another app is already reached at this address, or at a path this one would sit inside or around. |
| `STATE_AI_FUNCTION_ASSIGNED` | 409 | Another AI adapter already handles this AI function. Remove it from that adapter first. |
| `STATE_APP_EXITED` | 409 | The app started and then stopped, so the deploy has nothing to send traffic to. |
| `STATE_BACKUP_DECISION_REQUIRED` | 409 | The app has storage and the request did not say whether to keep a final backup of it (R-204, R-205). |
| `STATE_INVALID` | 409 | The object is in a state this action does not apply to. |
| `STATE_SET_AT_STARTUP` | 409 | This is declared in Pando's startup configuration and cannot be changed through the API while it is. |
| `BACKUP_DECRYPT_FAILED` | 422 | The backup could not be decrypted with the key supplied. |
| `BACKUP_INCOMPLETE` | 422 | The backup is missing part of what it claims to hold, so it was not applied (R-215). |
| `BUILD_FAILED` | 422 | The build ran and did not succeed. Its log is the answer. |
| `BUILD_LISTENS_ON_LOOPBACK` | 422 | The built app listens only on 127.0.0.1 inside its container, where nothing outside it can reach it. |
| `BUILD_TIMEOUT` | 422 | The build exceeded the time allowed for it (R-119). |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many attempts in a short time — at a passcode, for example. Wait a few minutes and try again. |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 | Pando failed in a way it did not expect. The request ID finds the log line. |
| `ADAPTER_FAILED` | 502 | The adapter was reached and failed. |
| `ADAPTER_REGISTRY_RATE_LIMITED` | 502 | A registry refused an image because this server, or the app's registry account, has downloaded too many images recently. The message says when it accepts downloads again, where the registry said. |
| `ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | The adapter needed for this is not configured or not reachable. |

bearerToken.description: A token minted from the console or with `pando token create`. A delegated token acts as the person who made it and is bounded by their live grants (R-058, R-059). A service token is its own principal and holds only what has been shared with it (R-060).

scimToken.description: An identity provider's SCIM token, from `POST /api/v1/identity-providers/{providerID}/scim-token`. Accepted by the SCIM endpoints only, and not a Pando token.

sessionCookie.description: How the console authenticates. Cookies in Pando's namespace never reach an app (R-173).
